why: I checked all five expect lines and their proofs. Each one can be checked at the PR head before merge. Lines 1–3 are concrete `node -e` commands against `./math.js` that pass or fail by exit code, so they have one answer. Line 4 runs `npm test` at the head, expects exit 0, then uses grep plus a reading to confirm a test calls `average([])` and asserts 0. That is a clear check one reader can do. Line 5 swaps in `git show 088f4f4:math.js` at the head and expects `npm test` to fail. The base commit is already in the repo's history, so this needs nothing that only exists after merge. No line depends on a release, deploy, published page or package version, and "Publishing a new package version" is listed as a non-goal. Every proof is a run done at the head, so the criterion holds for the whole output.
